rationale:
bugs_open/301, fix candidate 1 — the one the bug file prefers and the filing lane explicitly offered to whoever takes it (vigilant_designer_offer_analysis HANDOFF_2026-08-18: 'Take bugs_open/301').

THE PROBLEM, plainly. page-build-handler's owned-page refusal lives only in save_page_sections — the LAST step that touches the page. So a build item aimed at a pages.rebuild_policy='owned' page spawns page-content-writer (an LLM call), runs the internal-link-resolver, and is only THEN refused. The work is done and thrown away. bugs_open/301 measured 39 discarded chains in ~2.5 hours on one site. Re-verified live 2026-08-19 post-roll (v1.0.1314): the 10:18 UTC cluster shows a page-build-handler orchestration created 10:18:27 ending complete_error with a COMPLETED page-content-writer child (spawned 10:18:42) and COMPLETED internal-link-resolver child (10:19:16) beside it. [MEASURED 2026-08-19] 146 open findings on owned pages are routed at handler_agent='page-build-handler' right now — each is a guaranteed wasted chain under the current ordering, on a fleet that hit its Anthropic cap on 2026-08-14.

THE FIX. rebuild_policy is knowable the moment load_page_record (step 2) has loaded the page row; it is not consulted until step 12. This change adds ONE opt-in config key to the load_page_record action — refuse_owned_page, absent and therefore inert everywhere — and one migration (488) that names it on page-build-handler's load_page_record step and routes that step's error to mark_item_failed. When the key is set and the loaded page is owned, the action: (1) decides via pageIsOwnedForGuard, the estate's SINGLE ownership predicate (unified for bugs_open/208 at the council reuse_agent seat's own insistence — this change adds no second predicate); (2) files the same deduped owned_page_review row the save-path guard files, refused_by='load_page_record' (emitOwnedPageReviewItem, same item_key namespace, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so it converges with reconcile's and save's rows); (3) returns an error LEADING with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix — the exact marker update_work_item_status' owned_page_refusal_status (migration 480, live on v1.0.1314) matches in __step_error.message. The refusal therefore lands wont_fix, not failed, with ZERO new vocabulary: it composes with Tier 1 by construction, answering that submission's own risk 5 ('a reviewer should confirm the marker survives whatever step 301 moves the refusal to' — it leads the new error).

THE SAVE-PATH GUARD STAYS. It is the backstop for every other caller and for the early guard's fail-open window; removing it would re-open bugs_closed/295. The early guard fails OPEN on an unreadable policy, matching the predicate's posture — and cheaply here, because unlike the assemble-seam guard (which is the last line before a git commit and therefore logs its fail-open to agent_error_log), this one has the save guard downstream: an unchecked page costs at most one wasted chain, never a clobber.

THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM THAT LICENSES THE MOVE, and how it is being verified. Every content-writing path in page-build-handler's live workflow ends at save_page_sections. Read from the live agent_definitions row 2026-08-19: the only write path is validate_content -> save_sections -> update_status -> spawn_rerender_agent -> deploy_page (rerender/deploy sit AFTER the save, success arm only), and the non-write arms — check_page_found else, mark_no_ready_sections, mark_writer_skipped — park the item without touching the page. So an early refusal refuses exactly the population the save guard refuses today; it cannot cut off a legitimate owned-page write because the workflow contains none. The bug file's '74 completions on owned pages' is NOT counter-evidence: rebuild_policy is MUTABLE and those joins are query-time (the 277 lane's §8 correction — classify by the guard's error text, never the policy column), and the current graph has no bypass. A 090 diagnosis run was filed on exactly this question before this submission (intake 7281193f-59c2-489a-a9f2-fd4d58408cf5, run dd61df1b-0d93-46e6-9065-1e0b9623379a); its verdict will be read and recorded in the lane NOTES, and refutes-if-wrong the central premise.

WHY AN OPT-IN FIELD, AND THE CONSUMERS ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (owner rulings 2026-08-02 §2 and 2026-07-29 §3). [MEASURED 2026-08-19] exactly TWO live, non-snapshot, non-deleted agent_definitions carry a load_page_record step: page-build-handler and tool-recreation-handler. The second is the tool pipeline — the legitimate owner of owned pages, which must NEVER refuse them. That census is what forces the opt-in shape: a default-ON rule in code would have broken the tool pipeline on its next owned-page rebuild. One migration names one step; migration 488's verify block carries a negative control that ABORTS if any other live step acquires the key. Per the RFC_022 narrowing (owner ruling 2026-08-11): opt-in, unsafe side (OFF = today's waste, not a clobber risk) is the default, zero live consumers name it before the migration that ships with it — not architecture scope; this council round is the right venue.

ONE DECLARATION TRADE-OFF, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED. The key is declared in the spec's ConfigKeys, not Optional: it is a setting (a boolean read from config, like update_work_item_status' skip_if_missing), not a data reference, and ExtractActionInputs would treat an Optional entry as a path to resolve. The consequence: cmd/config-key-audit --optional-key-budget counts Optional ONLY (its own header: 'ConfigKeys is deliberately NOT counted'), so this key does not move load_page_record's budget count (3 of N=10). If the seat reading this thinks accumulated authority should count ConfigKeys too, that is a fair objection to the BUDGET TOOL and I will file it there — hiding was not the intent, which is why this paragraph exists.

NAMED BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, the honest list. (1) A genuine load_page_record error (DB failure, malformed authoritative id — bugs_open/220's fatal path) now routes error_step -> mark_item_failed: the item dies visibly failed, attempt counted, instead of failing the workflow. This ALIGNS the step with every sibling in this workflow (plan_sections, call_content_writer, save_sections, deploy_page all route there already) and is active from config-apply time on the old binary too. The 220 council's objection to a soft miss was that it routed through the SUCCESS-labelled path with the item untouched; routing through mark_item_failed marks the item failed first, which is the loud behaviour that objection asked for. (2) An owned-page item that would today take a no-op arm (mark_no_ready_sections / mark_writer_skipped, both parking at needs_human_review with a 'the target section was NOT rebuilt' message) is now refused up front: wont_fix + owned_page_review row. Both outcomes are visible parks that the promoter's floor ignores (it counts complete/verified/failed only — read from the live pre_query by the 277 lane 2026-08-18), so the gate arithmetic is unchanged; the refusal is the truer record and carries the fix pointer (spec.fix names apply_section_edit and the tool pipeline). (3) tool-recreation-handler: no change by construction — it does not carry the key, and the migration's negative control keeps it that way.

ORDERING, deliberately order-TOLERANT (no _HOLD, no loaded-gun pending state). Config before binary: LoadPageRecordInputSpec has CheckConfig without StrictConfig, so the old binary logs ONE deduped 'unrecognised config key' warning and ignores it (platform/validation/workflow.go:185-195 warns for non-strict actions, never rejects); only the error-routing alignment activates early. Binary before config: the code is dormant until the migration names the key. 488 is exercised: dry-run applied AND rolled back in one transaction against the live row (both NOTICEs fired), and the already-set guard proven able to fire by a double-apply probe that ABORTED with '488: refuse_owned_page is ALREADY set' — the control could have come out otherwise and did.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because it is the obvious objection. It repairs nothing and unblocks nothing: the ~146 queued findings will be refused CHEAPLY instead of expensively, not fixed. The routes that would fix them are owned elsewhere and deliberately not touched: Tier 2 (finding-to-edit conversion) is with the copy_quality_two_stage exchange, migration 473 (the 184 lane) covers literal_markdown deterministically, and bug 301's candidate 3 (producers should stop filing generic content items against owned pages at all) remains the real upstream repair. This change is the ordering half: stop paying for work the guard then throws away.

plan.summary: page-build-handler refuses an owned page at the LAST workflow step, after the LLM writer and link resolver have already run — 39 discarded chains in 2.5h measured, 146 findings queued behind the same waste today. This change teaches the load_page_record action an opt-in refuse_owned_page key (default OFF, inert everywhere): when set and the loaded page is rebuild_policy='owned', the action files the same deduped owned_page_review row the save-path guard files and errors with the OWNED_PAGE_GUARD marker leading, so the existing error_step -> mark_item_failed -> owned_page_refusal_status machinery (migration 480, live) stamps the item wont_fix. Migration 488 opts in exactly one step — page-build-handler.load_page_record — and routes its error to mark_item_failed. The save-path guard stays as the backstop. Of the two live carriers of this action, the other (tool-recreation-handler, the tool pipeline) never gets the key, enforced by the migration's negative control.

edits.rationale: Declare the new key where the action's config contract lives, so UnknownConfigKeys recognises it and the audit sees it. ConfigKeys not Optional: it is a setting, not a data reference — and the budget trade-off that choice carries is disclosed in the rationale rather than left to be discovered.
edits.sketch:
var LoadPageRecordInputSpec = datahelpers.ActionInputSpec{
 	CheckConfig: true,
 	Required:    []string{"site_id"},
 	Optional:    []string{"page_name", "page_id", "authoritative_page_id"},
+	// refuse_owned_page (bugs_open/301): when true, a loaded page whose
+	// pages.rebuild_policy is 'owned' is REFUSED here — before the content
+	// writer is spawned — instead of at save_page_sections ...
+	ConfigKeys: []string{"refuse_owned_page"},
 	Defaults:   map[string]interface{}{},
 	Deprecated: map[string]string{},
 }

edits.rationale: The mechanism. Both return paths (the authoritative-id path and the name/id path) route their found result through one helper, so the check cannot be reached on one path and missed on the other. Reuses the guard's three existing pieces — pageIsOwnedForGuard (the single predicate), emitOwnedPageReviewItem (the same deduped review row), ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix leading the error (the Tier 1 marker) — and adds no new vocabulary anywhere. Fail-open on an unreadable policy, logged at Warn: the save-path guard is still downstream, so the window costs one wasted chain at most, never a clobber.

Four cases, and the discrimination cases are what make it a control rather than a demonstration. (1) Key set + owned page: refused, review row filed, error LEADS with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix — asserted with strings.HasPrefix against the CONSTANT, so a rename of the marker goes red here rather than silently unstamping wont_fix. (2) Key set + generic page: proceeds, and ExpectationsWereMet proves no review row was filed. (3) KEY ABSENT + owned page: the mock expects ONLY the page lookup — a rebuild_policy read or an INSERT fails the test, pinning that the default path does not so much as read the policy (tool-recreation-handler's production case). (4) Policy read errors: fail-open, record returned, no review row. All pass; the package suite is green.

edits.rationale: The config half: the single deliberate opt-in, plus the error routing that makes the refusal land on the step already carrying owned_page_refusal_status=wont_fix. Guarded on the live shape: exactly one live row; the step runs the load_page_record action; the key is not already set; NO error_step already exists (another lane changing it aborts the migration); next_step is still check_page_found; and mark_item_failed still carries the Tier 1 key — WITHOUT which an early refusal would land failed and re-poison the promoter floor, so the guard makes 480-first a precondition rather than an assumption. Verify is DO/RAISE with a negative control asserting no other live step acquired the key. Exercised: dry-run apply+rollback in one rolled-back transaction (both NOTICEs fired); double-apply probe ABORTED on the already-set guard, proving the control can fire.

Deliberately leaves owned_page_review rows and wont_fix stamps already written: they are a true record of refusals that happened. After rollback the refusal happens at save_page_sections again — the waste returns, no protection is lost, because the save-path guard never moved.

plan.risks:
1. **The structural claim ('no write path bypasses save_sections') is the load-bearing premise.** It is read from the live workflow graph first-hand, and a 090 diagnosis run (dd61df1b) was filed on exactly this question before submission; its verdict is read and recorded either way. If the loop refutes it, this change is withdrawn or narrowed before the roll — the migration is unapplied-able (ROLLBACK file, exercised) and the Go half is inert without it.

2. **Genuine load errors change route** (workflow-fail -> mark_item_failed, failed, attempt counted). Aligns with every sibling step and satisfies the 220 council's loud-failure intent, but it IS a change to 220's error path: a malformed/deleted authoritative id now lands the item failed via the error arm rather than failing the saga. A reviewer who thinks the saga-failure path carried semantics the item-failure path does not (e.g. a dispatcher retry that only fires on saga failure) should say so — I did not find one.

3. **Owned-page items that today park needs_human_review via the no-op arms will instead land wont_fix + owned_page_review.** Gate-neutral (the promoter floor counts complete/verified/failed only) and truer, but it moves rows between two human-facing queues; whoever drains needs_human_review should not be surprised to see owned-page no-ops disappear from it after the next roll.

4. **The refusal is keyed on the same string marker as Tier 1** — a rename of ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix silently converts early refusals back to failed. Mitigated identically: the test asserts the prefix FROM the constant, and the constant's doc comment (corrected 2026-08-18) lists the matcher set. This change adds a fourth matcher; the comment should gain the line — noted as a follow-up edit in the same commit if a reviewer agrees it is worth the same-file touch (the comment lives in owned_page_guard.go, whose matcher list currently names three).

5. **Dead code risk in the no-op arms**: after this ships, mark_no_ready_sections / mark_writer_skipped can no longer be reached BY AN OWNED PAGE, but remain reachable by generic pages (writer skips, empty specs) — they are not dead and are not touched.

6. **Emission volume**: an owned page whose finding is re-dispatched repeatedly now emits the review item on every early refusal instead of every late one — same rate, earlier; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING converges to one open row per page, same as today.
